overall: AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the August 14, 2014 executive session discussed only contract renewal terms under Purpose 2, and the overheard talk was after the meeting without a quorum. Minutes and notice concerns were noted as reminders only.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Aug. 14, 2014 executive session improperly discussed the superintendent's professional competence and discipline without giving him Purpose 1 notice and rights.
allegations.key_passage: we nevertheless find the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law because the Board did not discuss these matters in executive session on August 14, 2014.

allegations.summary: A consultant overheard board members discussing the superintendent's performance outside the executive session, suggesting the discussion occurred improperly among members.
allegations.key_passage: the conversation that Mr. Dyer overheard appears to have occurred after the meeting and did not involve a quorum of the Board.

allegations.summary: Not alleged in the complaint; the AG noted the executive session minutes were too sparse, consisting of a single sentence stating the topic.
allegations.key_passage: We remind the Board that a public body must create and maintain accurate minutes of all meetings, including executive sessions

allegations.summary: Not alleged; the AG noted the executive session notice did not name the specific non-union personnel with whom the board was negotiating.
allegations.key_passage: a public body must identify the specific non-union personnel or collective bargaining unit with which it is negotiating in its meeting notice
